notes: PETTY CASH NOW CHARGES THE DEPARTMENT THAT SPENT THE MONEY. Until now every reimbursed float was charged org-wide — to "School" — no matter which department's imprest had spent it. A department's tea, taxis and stationery never reached its own report and the budget it was spending against never moved. Three things caused it and all three are fixed. A float must now be told which unit it belongs to, and the picker asks instead of quietly answering "School" for you. A petty cash voucher now carries a Charge to unit and a project, filled in from the float the moment you pick it. And the budget warning now measures the expense against the budget it will actually post to, rather than against the org-wide row. YOUR EXISTING RECORDS ARE CORRECTED TOO. This update re-scopes the reimbursements already on the ledger onto the departments that spent them. It moves nothing else — not one amount, account, date or voucher link is touched — and it is exactly reversible. Only reimbursements that are unambiguous are corrected: the batch must belong to a single float, that float must have a unit, and every line must still be unscoped. A reversal is corrected together with the voucher it reverses, so a cancelled reimbursement can never leave expenditure stranded on a department. PLEASE TAKE A BACKUP BEFORE YOU UPDATE, AND ANOTHER AFTER. This release changes the shape of stored data, so a backup taken before the update restores the OLD structure — the app will tell you as much on the dashboard until you take a fresh one. Backup & Export, Back up now. RETIRE A FLOAT ON THE DAY IT WAS RETIRED. Closing a float now asks for the date the cash actually went back, like funding and reimbursement already did. Closing on 3 January for a year that ended 31 December used to post the return in January, leaving December showing cash still in the tin, and put the deposit into the wrong month's bank reconciliation. THE RETIREMENT STATEMENT NOW SHOWS WHAT THE MONEY WAS SPENT ON. A voucher split across two expense heads is listed as the two expenses it was, instead of all of it against the first account. Underneath, a new Analysis by expenditure head totals the claim by account — the figure a retirement is actually approved against — beside the imprest reconciliation. Long schedules keep their reconciliation and signatures together on the closing page. MONTH-END NOW ASKS ABOUT YOUR FLOATS. The month-end checklist lists any float still holding expenditure it has not retired, so a month is not signed off over a custodian's uncleared tin. It is advisory — carrying a float across a month end is normal. PRINTED REPORTS SIT PROPERLY ON THE PAGE AGAIN. The audit log, group overview and opening balances printed at screen spacing and ran to more sheets than they needed. The setting meant to tighten them had never taken effect.
